title: SQLITE: SQLiteDialect.get_check_constraints incorrectly reflects multiline check constraints

labels.name: reflection
labels.description: reflection of tables, columns, constraints, defaults, sequences, views, everything else

labels.name: quagmire
labels.description: really hard to make the issue work "correctly" without lots of complication, risk

labels.name: law of twos
labels.description: the law that issues about a particular topic come in twos

body:
### Describe the bug

The `get_check_constraints` method of SQLiteDialect, does not correctly handle multi line CHECK constraints in SQLAlchemy reflection. When performing a alembic batch_op for example, multi line check constraints will not be or wrongly reflected and can result in SQL errors.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

1.3.18

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

pysqlite

### Database Vendor and Major Version

SQLite

### Python Version

3.8.10

### Operating system

Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, MetaData, Table, Column, Integer, CheckConstraint
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()


class Example(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'example'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    value = Column(Integer)

    __table_args__ = (
        CheckConstraint("""((value > 0) AND
             (value < 100))"""),
    )


# Create an in-memory SQLite database and create the table
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:')
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

# Reflect the metadata to get the table object
metadata = MetaData()
metadata.reflect(bind=engine)
example_table = Table('example', metadata, autoload_with=engine)

# Print the CheckConstraints before deletion
print("Constraints before deletion:")
for constraint in example_table.constraints:
    if isinstance(constraint, CheckConstraint):
        print(f"CheckConstraint: {constraint.sqltext}")

# Drop the existing table
Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)

# Recreate the table based on reflected metadata
metadata.create_all(engine)
```

### Additional context

The solution to this problem is editing the regex to match check constraints:

```py
@reflection.cache
def get_check_constraints(self, connection, table_name, schema=None, **kw):
    table_data = self._get_table_sql(
        connection, table_name, schema=schema, **kw
    )
    if not table_data:
        return []

    CHECK_PATTERN = r"(?:CONSTRAINT (\w+) +)?" r"CHECK *\( *((.|\n)+?) *\)(, ?\n|\n) *" # new
    check_constraints = []
    # NOTE: we aren't using re.S here because we actually are
    # taking advantage of each CHECK constraint being all on one
    # line in the table definition in order to delineate. This
    # necessarily makes assumptions as to how the CREATE TABLE
    # was emitted.
    for match in re.finditer(CHECK_PATTERN, table_data, re.I):
        check_constraints.append(
            {"sqltext": match.group(2), "name": match.group(1)}
        )

    return check_constraints
```

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/881be0a21633b3fee101cb34cc611904b8cba618/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/sqlite/base.py#L2620C1-L2620C77

This line is not changed in the latest version
